items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear (bgr24ToYv12, yuvToRgbUnscaled, dst_r_idx), but there are long runs of b00/g01/r11 variables. Fixed-point math like `>> 15) + 16` and `+ 128` has no comments, and the RY/GY constants don't point to their FFmpeg counterparts.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: yuvToRgbUnscaled is about 90 lines, and its odd-width tail repeats the main loop body. The kernels are plain scalar loops, not the shared @Vector helpers the conventions ask for. Build output was committed: .zig-cache/h/*.txt (859 lines) and zig-out/lib/libswscale_candidate.so.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The process dispatch returns without converting anything when a guard fails, e.g. `(w & 1) == 0` for bgr24->yuv420p and `(h & 1) == 0` for yuv->rgb, so the output is silently left unwritten. Strides go through `@intCast(src_stride[0])` with no validation. Magic constants 15/16/128 are used inline.

items.name: Geometry, stride and tail handling
items.name_zh: 几何尺寸、步长与尾部处理
items.evidence: Odd-height YUV->RGB and odd-width BGR24->YUV420P paths are skipped entirely. On odd height, bgr24ToYv12 writes only luma for the last row, with no chroma. No SIMD or tail strategy is visible. The hidden correctness test failed.

items.name: ABI and build-target conformance

items.evidence: The shown diff doesn't include build.zig or the exported signatures, so I can't confirm them. The .so builds and the dispatch path exists. Shipping the built binary and zig-cache in the workspace is untidy, but it isn't an ABI problem.
